newsitem.title: USA: Surgical Laser gets partial judgement.
newsitem.headline: Surgical Laser gets partial judgement.

text.p: Surgical Laser Technologies Inc said Wednesday that the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania granted the company's motion for partial summary judgment in the suit brought by inventor Norio Daikuzono.
Surgical Laser said the court ruled it does not owe Daikuzono, the inventor of three of the company's patents in contact laser technology, any salary under an earlier company employment arrangement.
The court ruled that the statute of limitations bars any claim by Daikuzono for allegedly unpaid royalties accruing before February 1991, according to the company.
The court also ruled that no royalties were owed to Daikuzono from the settlement proceeds received by the company from Sharplan Lasers Inc in December 1995, according to the company.
The company reiterated its belief that "it has meritorious defenses" against the inventor's claims for royalties accruing after February 1991 and for patent infringement.

The suit was started in February 1995 in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio, but was transferred to the Eastern District of Pennsylvania in February 1996, according to the company. Surgical Laser filed its motion for partial summary judgment in May 1996.
The trial of the remaining issues was expected to take place in 1997.
Surgical Laser manufactures and markets lasers and disposable Contact Laser(TM) Delivery Systems, which can be used in virtually all general and specialty surgical procedures.
